description: Multiplicative adjustments applied to base-rate LOA for each modality. Values are point estimates inside published BIO/Informa ranges; range_low/range_high preserve the documented uncertainty for sensitivity analysis.

multipliers.rationale: Reference modality. Most BIO/Informa base rates are computed on a small-molecule-dominant historical cohort.
mAbs show higher Phase 1 safety and lower attrition through approval; biologics LOA from P1 reported ~11% vs ~6% for NMEs.
ADCs face higher CMC and DLT/payload-toxicity attrition relative to naked antibodies; manufacturing complexity raises late-stage risk.
Gene therapies show elevated Phase 3 attrition (durability, immunogenicity, dose-response); CMC scale-up risk also significant.
Autologous cell therapies face per-patient manufacturing variability and complex logistics; documented higher commercial-stage attrition.
Allogeneic platforms simplify supply but face persistence and immunogenicity risk.
Platform validated for vaccines; therapeutic mRNA still has limited Phase 3 readouts outside infectious disease.
Recombinant proteins/enzymes track biologics behavior with slight discount for immunogenicity risk.
ASO/siRNA approvals exist but historical Phase 2 attrition is high; delivery/biodistribution remains the dominant risk.
Peptides behave like small molecules in success rates; PK/PD challenges offset structural simplicity.
Unspecified modality — defaults to reference; widen the range to reflect higher prior uncertainty.
